key_insight: Optimizing the cavity shape for capillary auto-ejection can produce centimeter-sized drops that relax to near-spherical form faster, with a shallow central depression outperforming the surface-area-minimizing parabolic design.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical design rule for passive drop generators in drop-tower microgravity experiments, where only seconds are available to create usable relaxed liquid spheres.
method: Studied capillary auto-ejection (puddle jumping) as a passive drop-generation mechanism.
Analyzed parabolic cross-section cavities filled with fixed liquid volume to identify the shape minimizing initial surface area.
Used smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to compare post-ejection relaxation times, including a modified cavity with a shallow central depression.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based evaluation showing that the surface-area-minimizing parabolic cavity also minimizes relaxation time within that family, and that adding a shallow central depression reduces relaxation time further.
watch_item: The best-performing shape increases initial surface area, so the gain in relaxation speed may come with trade-offs in fabrication complexity or robustness.
paper_title: Rapid generation of relaxed centimeter-sized drops by capillary auto-ejection
